correctness.rationale: Contracting the open paths formed by two prescribed images gives a bijection from completions to permutations on n−2 objects, adding only the already forced cycles. Among inverted ordered image pairs the two possible fixed points and the two-cycle contribute (a−1)+(n−b)+1=n−(b−a). Hence E[C_n I_{a,b}]=H_{n−2}/2+(n−(b−a))/(n(n−1)), and subtracting H_n/2 verifies the local covariance, including n=2 with H_0=0. Dividing by P(I=1)=1/2 gives the conditional mean. The weighted sum over distances yields −(2n−1)/12, and finite differentiation of the normalized Mallows weight gives q^{-1} Cov_q(C_n,Inv_n). The beta expansion follows at fixed n by the chain rule with q=e^{−beta}.
residual_risks: The recorded finite checks are corroboration, not the proof for arbitrary n. The Taylor remainder is for fixed n.

evidence: Gladkich–Peled, Theorem 1.5, estimates the total mean by order of magnitude across Mallows regimes. He–Müller–Verstraaten, abstract and Theorem 1.1, treat limiting cycle counts at fixed q<1; the limiting fixed-point mean near q=1 even illustrates a noncommutation of limits.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These inspected asymptotic statements do not imply the finite-n slope or any individual positional term. The direct indexed match, not the broader Mallows literature, decides coverage.
